title: Course ownership sharing and learner continuity policy
status: Draft for Johan and Jorrie to approve
body:
Purpose and authority
This policy governs the offering of published courses between APGI and partner training platforms. It separates copyright ownership, platform operation, course publication and learner entitlements. The draft requires approval by Johan and Jorrie before adoption. It does not change any existing agreed price, financial approval or live-payment setting.

1 Ownership and initial publication
The declared legal course owner controls sharing. Developing, paying to host, branding or administering a course does not by itself transfer copyright. An APGI-owned course is reviewed and published on APGI before being offered to a partner. A course developed for a client as declared owner starts privately on that client platform. That client decides whether to offer its published course to APGI or another partner. A partner-developed course follows the same rule. Drafts must not be distributed as public shared courses. An ownership transfer requires separately recorded authority.

2 Private shelf and recipient consent
Sharing creates a private shelf offer, not an automatic portfolio publication, learner enrolment, file export or public-folder copy. The recipient owner receives an in-platform message and tracked email. The offer identifies the course owner, published release, content fingerprint, rights and approved cost schedule where available. The recipient previews the course and may accept and publish it into its own portfolio or decline it. Existing explicitly authorised VPSHR Level 0 publication for NKS Capital and Mediation Zone is retained. Prior reviews remain evidence; publication on another platform does not invent a new content approval.

3 Prices and locked obligations
APGI and partner owners use the same versioned calculator. The approved owner schedule, route, quantity, currency, platform costs, processing provision and recipient allocations are the price basis. For an APGI course sold by a partner, the design allocation is 80 percent selling partner and 20 percent APGI. For another partner-owned course sold by a different partner, it is 80 percent course owner, 10 percent selling platform and 10 percent APGI. Existing approved exceptions remain recorded separately. APGI and SRMS retain their agreed 50/50 allocation of the relevant net platform income.

A recipient can reduce only its own selling margin. An example is an approved 100 dollar content amount split 80 dollars seller and 20 dollars APGI: a 10 dollar seller discount leaves APGI at 20 dollars and the seller at 70 dollars. Platform and processing amounts remain additional and locked. APGI income is not recalculated as a percentage of the reduced buyer total. Discounts cannot produce a negative selling margin or consume owner income or platform costs. The existing quantity discount algorithms remain unchanged. Single-course distribution requires an approved single-course schedule. Category wallets need an approved category-wide rights and allocation schedule; a one-course licence cannot create unrestricted wallet rights. Unapproved pricing remains planning only.

4 Partner branding and communications
The recipient controls its own branding and verified sender configuration. Sample email designs are provided and may be edited in Email management and email sets. Changes do not permit sender spoofing, misstatement of ownership or removal of required privacy information. Provider acceptance, delivery, opening and completion of an in-platform action are distinct events. Messages and attempts remain auditable and retries must be idempotent.

5 Content protection and monitoring
Course packages remain behind authenticated entitlement checks. Shared offerings reference the owner's published release; they do not provide the receiving platform with an unrestricted public download or source-authoring right. Rights holders must agree any separate permission to edit or redistribute source material. Existing learner edition pins, progress checks and assessment rules remain in force. Screen capture and manual copying cannot be made impossible; the platform must not promise absolute copy protection.

Monitoring records bounded counts of denied course-file requests in ten-minute windows. Twenty or more verified-user denials in a window raise a deduplicated message and email for the owner to investigate. These cross-platform alerts contain course identifiers, counts and times, not learner identities, assessments, passwords, tokens or IP addresses. A signal is not proof of misuse. Human review is required before a correction notice or withdrawal decision. The system does not revoke access automatically on suspicion. Detailed access and retention arrangements remain subject to the platform privacy policy and applicable agreements.

6 Three notice withdrawal process
First notice: the owner records the concern, supporting evidence, required remedy and a response deadline. The recipient receives an inter-platform message and tracked email.
Second notice: after the first response deadline, and if the issue remains unresolved, the owner records why improvement is insufficient and issues a final request to correct it. The message warns that new course access may be withdrawn and records a second response deadline.
Third notice: after the final deadline, the owner explicitly confirms withdrawal and its reason. New sales, learner invitations and enrolments for that course on the receiving platform are stopped. The notices and receipts remain in the audit history. The default response window is seven calendar days at each correction stage and may be set from one to thirty days when the notice is issued. No scheduled process silently escalates a notice. Legal emergencies require a separate agreed incident process rather than disguising an immediate withdrawal as completion of these three steps.

7 Existing learner continuity
Withdrawal from the partner's new business does not revoke the rights of learners already enrolled there. At withdrawal, the platform records the enrolled learners entitled to continue. Their original course edition, access expiry, progress, assessment results and certificate rights remain intact. Each affected learner receives an individual message and email explaining that the course is no longer offered to new learners on that platform, but their existing enrolment may be completed there. They may contact their administrator to arrange access on another approved production platform. A destination must be verified and the necessary privacy and consent steps completed before any transfer; production learners must never be moved into a staging environment. No automatic alternative account or extra enrolment is implied. Expired or separately revoked learner entitlements do not become valid again.

8 Common platform releases
APGI V2 and partner deployments use one versioned application release, including the calculator and review capabilities. Company data, branding, domains, sender settings and access permissions remain separate. A release coordinator prepares the same source overlay for every registered deployment, requires all builds to be ready, verifies the target versions, and records deployment identifiers and rollback evidence. A failed target prevents planned promotion; a promotion failure triggers rollback of already promoted targets where possible. Separate promotions are not a distributed atomic transaction and any incomplete rollback must be escalated. Version mismatch blocks course exchange and is reported for investigation. New partner deployments must be added to the release registry and verified before activation. Mediation Zone currently uses its APGI V2 workspace; no separate production training deployment is assumed.

9 Version changes and preserved evidence
Sharing freezes the owner publication and pricing basis. A replacement course edition or commercial schedule requires an explicit replacement offer and recipient decision; it must not overwrite existing learner pins, prior approvals or an accepted commercial agreement. Earlier course releases, review responses, endorsements, email attempts, notices and certificates are retained. Opening a message, shelving a course or running an automated check does not count as human approval.

10 Approval and operational readiness
Johan and Jorrie approve this exact policy and applicable commercial schedules. Partner owners approve their own portfolio publication and margin decisions within the fixed obligations. Live payments remain disabled until separately authorised and tested. Before enabling general course exchange, test owner authority, draft isolation, private shelf visibility, partner acceptance, protected allocations, notice order, blocked new enrolments, continuing learner access, email tracking and release-version consistency.
